open_points.subject: Refusal write semantics across multi-change operations
open_points.text: "A refusal writes nothing" ... and ... "When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay"
open_points.question: When an operation returns `internal_error` after earlier successful store changes in the same request, is that response still treated as a refusal that writes nothing, or as an error after partial committed progress?
options: All prior store changes in the same request must be rolled back so no writes remain on any refusal.
Earlier successful store changes remain committed; only the failing change writes nothing.
Different behavior by operation type (single-change vs multi-change).
open_points.default_guess: Earlier successful store changes remain committed; only the failing store change is absent.

open_points.subject: How callers obtain a SpooledFile identity for `read_spooled_file`
open_points.text: "a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through `read_spooled_file`" and `read_spooled_file` "names it by its identity — `run_id`, `producer_node_id`, `map_index`, `attempt_number`, `producer_port`, `list_index`"
open_points.question: Which surfaced read outputs must include the full SpooledFile identity tuple so the owner can actually call `read_spooled_file` without guessing?
options: Every place that returns a SpooledFile fact must include full identity fields.
Only trace/NodeExecution reads include full identity; other views expose digest/size/media_type only.
Introduce a separate lookup operation from digest/facts to SpooledFile identity.
open_points.default_guess: Include full SpooledFile identity in trace/approval-related owner-visible records wherever a spooled file is referenced.
